=== Original heirship deed — 30 October 2026 ===
Elijah’s existing father [[Glascow-14|Isaac Glasgow]] is now assessed at '''97% confident inference''', superseding the earlier 36% review. The original Weakley deed names Elijah among “the heirs of Isaac Glasgow deceased” and conveys land originally surveyed in Isaac’s name. Numerous coheirs match the existing family, including William C., Wagstaff K., John G., Joseph D. and Jesse Glasgow, with initialled Glasgow heirs and the Coffe and Adams couples.<ref name="WeakleyHeirs1851">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSKJ-RS12-5 Weakley County Register of Deeds, pp. 410–411], DGS 008151469, image 213. Deed dated 20 February 1851, execution/delivery and acknowledgment 14 March, registered 15 March 1851. Original visually inspected30October 2026; selected kinship, signature and acknowledgment passages checked, not a full metes-and-bounds transcription.</ref>

The deed states heirship, not a literal son clause; fatherhood is a confident inference from the particular family group. The grantors include husbands, so they are not all biological sons. The initialled heirs and the possible duplicate [[Glasgow-116]]/[[Glasgow-2613]] accounts remain separately qualified. [[Glasgow-118|Elias]] is not securely named and is not excluded by absence. Other clearly matched coheirs receive separate assessments; mothers and vital fields remain unchanged.

The already cited marriage index places Isaac Glascoe with Dosha Kanaday at Wake on 7 September 1812.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F8TM-BLQ North Carolina, Marriages, 1759–1979], Isaac Glascoe and Dosha Kanaday, 7 September 1812, Wake. Index inspected30October 2026; original image unavailable in this viewer.</ref> Smith’s published obituary abstract reports Isaac’s Currituck origin, move to Weakley in 1826 and death there 9 June 1848.<ref>Jonathan K.T. Smith, [https://tngenweb.org/records/davidson/obits/nca/nca47-08.htm Genealogical Abstracts from Reported Deaths, Nashville Christian Advocate 1847–1849] (2003), abstract p. 54, notice under 27 October 1848. Original newspaper uninspected; the abstract page is not the newspaper page.</ref> These support the family route and replace the earlier unsupported geographic objection. They do not independently name Elijah’s parents. Existing birth/death fields and upstream ancestry remain unchanged.
